reports.report: I derived the sum formula for $S = \sum_{a,b=1}^N \lfloor ab/(N+1) \rfloor$ in terms of $f(M) = \sum_{a,b=1}^{M-1} (ab \pmod M)$ where $M = N+1$. The given sum $S = (N^3-N^2+2)/4$ was equivalent to the condition $f(M) = M^2(M-2)/2$, which simplifies to Pillai's arithmetical function $G(M) = \sum_{k=1}^M \gcd(k, M) = 2M$. Using the multiplicative property of $G(M)$, I showed that the only solution is $M=4$, yielding $N=3$.
